title: Migration Playbook: Versioned API Signals & Safe-Deprecation Workflows
creator: Sana Patel
description: Create a pragmatic, engineering-friendly migration playbook that surfaces explicit version signals, catalogs behavior flags, and defines safe deprecation workflows for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. The playbook should be consumable by SDK teams, solutions engineers, and customer success; include migration guides for client libraries, rollout templates (canary/shadow/cutover), and a repeatable backward-compatibility test suite used by runtime and model onboarding teams.
acceptance_criteria: Author comprehensive migration guide in Confluence that covers: version header semantics, flag behavior (legacy_streaming_mode, structured_output_v2), and example client migrations for Node/Python/Go.
Define and implement a compatibility test harness that can replay historical streaming sessions and compare token-by-token and event boundaries against golden outputs.
Create a rollout plan template with metrics, guardrails, and automatic fallback triggers for 2-stage canary + shadow validation.
Publish SDK feature flags and deprecation timeline with automated opt-in toggles for early adopters.
Verify end-to-end signoff from runtime, SDK, DX, and security teams in a cross-team review checklist.

updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, SDK, DX, and Security. Agreed on version signal header 'x-rw-api-version' and a short numeric versioning scheme (major.minor).
2026-02-28: Runtime team prototype accepts behavior flags via header and request param. Early trade-off discussion: header vs request body flag — chose header for routing simplicity.
2026-03-05: DX draft for Node SDK flag API posted. Internal feedback: prefer explicit opt-in method rather than global client config to avoid unintended rollouts.
2026-03-09: Decided to implement 'shadow validation' for 2 weeks before any client-facing deprecation notice. Added ENG-8422 as dependency to reuse existing compatibility probes.
2026-03-12: Security review scoping started; no cryptographic changes anticipated. Security requested a design for audit logging of flag changes (added as follow-up).
2026-03-14: PM review with Legal and Customer Success completed; migration timeline draft ready for stakeholder review in the 2026-03-16 All-Hands.
decisions: Version signal is orthogonal to model selection; it only toggles API behavior semantics (stream framing, function-call contract, structured output strictness).
Behavior flags will be surfaced as both header ('x-rw-behavior') and explicit SDK opt-in calls; gateway will honor header if present but SDKs will emit warnings for deprecated client-side flags.
Deprecation cadence: 90-day opt-in window -> 60-day shadow validation -> 30-day warning -> 180-day full removal; timeline customizable per-release in release notes.
Fallback policy for incompatible clients: preserve best-effort backward semantics for generation and emit structured parse-error telemetry rather than hard-failing unless 'strict_mode' is requested.
Compatibility tests must include both token-level diff and event-boundary diffs for streaming to catch off-by-one framing regressions.
risks: Mis-specified behavior flags could cause subtle semantic changes that only appear on long-running conversations; mitigated via shadow-run and longer golden-session corpus.
Customer SDKs that set global flags could accidentally opt-in many apps; mitigated by explicit per-call opt-in and developer warnings in npm/pypi releases.
Telemetry blind spots during canary — added instrumentation tasks to ensure rollouts are measurable at token and session granularity.
Coordination overhead across runtime, SDKs, and Solutions teams could prolong timelines if not synced — weekly cross-team sync mandated.
